backend-section.title: Voice model and external API (menu: Voice model / Text model)

about-version.description:
Version: 0.2.0
Author: H234598
Cinnamon-native voice typing for Fedora Cinnamon.

main-menu-settings-map.description: All persistent settings from the applet menu are available here. Recording options are in Recording, output and Auto-Submitt are in Text output, personal context and vocabulary are in Personalization, text polishing prompts are in Text polishing, and voice/backend values are in Voice model and external API. Dynamic actions such as downloading models, opening transcript folders, listing or exporting transcript documents, diagnostics, cleanup, and alarm commands remain in the applet panel menu.

primary-language-keybinding.description: Start dictation with the primary language
primary-language-keybinding.tooltip: Optional Cinnamon global shortcut. When already recording, it stops the current recording without changing its language.

secondary-language-keybinding.description: Start dictation with the secondary language
secondary-language-keybinding.tooltip: Optional Cinnamon global shortcut. When already recording, it stops the current recording without changing its language.

cancel-keybinding.tooltip: Optional Cinnamon global shortcut. Cancels the current recording, deletes local recording artifacts, and prevents auto-relisten restart.

show-panel-label.description: Show status text in the panel

auto-transcribe-timeout.description: Transcribe automatically at the time limit
auto-transcribe-timeout.tooltip: When a live applet recording reaches the maximum length, start transcription without requiring another shortcut press.

auto-relisten.tooltip: When automatic transcription finishes after a time limit, immediately start a new recording with the same duration. Manual stop or cancel does not restart recording.

keep-recording-artifacts.tooltip: Disabled by default for privacy. Temporary WAV/log files are still used while recording, then removed after a successful transcription.

input-device.tooltip: Optional PipeWire/Pulse source name. Max 4096 chars. Leave empty for the current default. Run 'speed-of-cinnamon list-inputs --json' to inspect available sources.

personalization-help.description: Personal context is background for recognition and polishing, for example preferred language, domain, product names, or style constraints. Custom vocabulary is a word list for spellings that should be recognized or preserved, for example project names, commands, abbreviations, file names, or proper nouns. Do not store secrets, passwords, API keys, account data, or other highly sensitive values here; these values may be sent to the configured transcription or polishing backend.

blacklist-help.description: Voice-activated blacklist: dictate 'blacklisteintrag: <word>' to add a word to the local blacklist without copying or auto-submitting that directive. Dictate 'Blacklist anzeigen' or a similar request to open the blacklist file for review and editing. If a blacklist hit is detected after transcription, the text is passed through the safety parser before clipboard or paste output so sensitive words can be masked.

personal-context.tooltip: Optional private context for recognition and text polishing. Use this for domain, style, product terms, or other background that should influence the transcript. Max 4096 chars. Available as {context}, {prompt}, and SPEED_OF_CINNAMON_CONTEXT.

vocabulary.tooltip: Optional custom terms, one per line, that should be recognized or preserved more reliably. Use this for product names, abbreviations, spellings, and proper nouns. Max 4096 chars. Available as {vocabulary}, {prompt}, and SPEED_OF_CINNAMON_VOCABULARY.

notify-recording.description: Notify when recording starts or reaches the time limit

append-space.description: Append a space after inserted text

sanitize-special-chars.tooltip: Optional compatibility fallback for direct typing on X11. Clipboard output normally works better with this disabled.

soften-profanity.tooltip: When enabled, common German and English profanity is replaced locally with harmless equivalents before transcripts are saved, copied, pasted, or auto-submitted. Disabled by default to avoid changing dictated code, commands, or exact quotes.

show-profanity-filter-list.tooltip: Create if needed and open the editable local profanity replacement file. Format: text -> replacement. Bundled entries may use trusted regex syntax; custom entries are treated as literal text for safety.

max-transcript-files.description: Keep a maximum of transcript files
max-transcript-files.tooltip: After each successful transcription, delete older transcript files so at most this many transcript files are kept. Preview cleanup and Clean old files use the same limit.

auto-paste-window-title.tooltip: Built-in marker names match known window classes/app IDs; codex and custom strings match the full window title case-insensitively. Matching targets receive a trailing Enter after Clipboard and paste. Empty disables Auto-Submitt. Max 4096 chars.

cli-path.tooltip: Optional override. Leave empty to use ~/.local/bin/speed-of-cinnamon when installed for the user, then /usr/bin/speed-of-cinnamon from the RPM/system install.

transcriber.tooltip: Automatic uses the selected Voice model to choose the local engine. Leave this on Automatic unless you need a command override.

whisper-model.tooltip: Model selected from the Voice menu, or a custom local model file or directory. Max 4096 chars.

transcriber-command.tooltip: Used by the Custom command transcriber, or by Automatic when filled. Max 4096 chars. The template is executed as arguments (no shell expansion), with direct support for `&&`-chained commands only. Placeholders: {audio}, {language}, {text}, {output_dir}, {output_base}, {context}, {vocabulary}, {prompt}. The command must print the transcript or write it to {text}.

post-process-backend.tooltip: Optional cleanup after ASR. Command runs a custom command template. Ollama uses a local model; OpenAI-compatible API can target compatible endpoints.

text-polishing-help.description: Text polishing runs after speech recognition and before clipboard/paste output. Presets provide safe reusable instructions: minimal corrections, natural text, command/code preservation, chat message, email, or sensitive-data masking. The custom instruction narrows the preset, for example tone, formatting, or app-specific requirements. Prefer precise instructions such as 'do not add content' or 'preserve commands exactly'.
text-polishing-help.tooltip: This section controls what happens after speech recognition but before the text reaches the clipboard, paste target, or Auto-Submitt. Choose a preset for the general behavior, then use the custom instruction and safety switches to narrow it. Keep instructions short and explicit. Avoid secrets in prompts because external polishing backends may receive the transcript, context, vocabulary, and effective polishing instruction.

post-process-preset.tooltip: Reusable instruction sent to Ollama, OpenAI-compatible text polishing, or the {prompt} placeholder of a custom command.

post-process-preset-help-minimal.description: Safe default fixes punctuation, capitalization, and obvious transcription errors without changing meaning.
post-process-preset-help-minimal.tooltip: Use this for normal dictation when you want the text cleaned up but not rewritten. The backend should correct punctuation, capitalization, spacing, and clear ASR mistakes only. It should preserve wording, intent, tone, technical terms, and factual content.

post-process-preset-help-clean.description: Clean natural text makes dictated text read naturally while preserving technical terms.
post-process-preset-help-clean.tooltip: Use this when raw dictation should become smoother prose. It may remove obvious filler words, repair sentence boundaries, and improve readability, but it should not invent facts, change meaning, or normalize commands and technical names incorrectly.

post-process-preset-help-code.description: Preserve commands and code keeps commands, paths, flags, identifiers, and quoted text exact.
post-process-preset-help-code.tooltip: Use this for terminals, developer chats, notes with shell commands, file paths, code snippets, variables, branch names, issue IDs, and quoted strings. It tells the backend to avoid typographic quotes and to keep syntax-sensitive text unchanged.

post-process-preset-help-chat.description: Short chat message formats a concise chat message without adding a greeting, subject, or sign-off.
post-process-preset-help-chat.tooltip: Use this for messengers and team chat. It should make the message compact and readable, but should not add salutations, signatures, headings, explanations, or context that was not dictated.

post-process-preset-help-email.description: Polite email formats an email while preserving dictated intent and content.
post-process-preset-help-email.tooltip: Use this for longer messages that should read like an email. It may improve structure and politeness, but should only add an opening or closing if the dictation clearly asks for one or already implies one.

post-process-preset-help-safety.description: Sensitive-data masking asks the backend to mask tokens, passwords, account data, phone numbers, addresses, and private names.
post-process-preset-help-safety.tooltip: Use this when dictated text might contain secrets or personal information. The backend should mask likely tokens, passwords, API keys, account data, contact details, addresses, and private names before output while preserving the rest of the text.

post-process-preset-help-custom.description: Custom instruction only uses your custom instruction without adding a preset.
post-process-preset-help-custom.tooltip: Use this when the preset instructions are too broad and you want the custom instruction field to define the whole polishing behavior. The global safety checkboxes still add their instructions when enabled.

post-process-preserve-code.tooltip: Keep commands, paths, filenames, flags, variable names, identifiers, code, and quoted text exact unless explicitly requested otherwise.

post-process-never-add-content.tooltip: Forbid extra facts, explanations, greetings, sign-offs, headings, or other content that was not dictated or explicitly requested.

post-process-mask-sensitive-data.tooltip: Ask the polishing backend to mask tokens, passwords, account data, phone numbers, addresses, and private names before output.

post-process-command.tooltip: Used when Text polishing is Custom command. Max 4096 chars. It receives the transcript on stdin and must print the final text. The template is executed as arguments (no shell expansion), with direct support for `&&`-chained commands only. Placeholders: {text}, {language}, {context}, {vocabulary}, {prompt}.

ollama-url.tooltip: Local Ollama base URL used when Text polishing is Ollama local model. Max 4096 chars.

ollama-model.tooltip: Model name for local Ollama polishing, for example llama3.2:3b or mistral. Max 4096 chars.

openai-compatible-url.tooltip: OpenAI-compatible base URL used for External API speech recognition and OpenAI-compatible text polishing. Defaults to OpenAI. Hosted or self-managed compatible endpoints can also be used. Max 4096 chars.

openai-compatible-model.tooltip: Model name for External API speech recognition. Text polishing can use a separate model. Max 4096 chars.

openai-compatible-text-model.tooltip: Model name for OpenAI-compatible text polishing. Defaults to gpt-4o-mini. Max 4096 chars.

openai-compatible-flex-processing.tooltip: Use OpenAI Flex processing for OpenAI API speech-to-text and text polishing requests. This adds service_tier=flex only for api.openai.com calls.

openai-compatible-api-key.tooltip: Optional Bearer token for External API speech recognition and text polishing. Leave empty only for endpoints that do not require authentication. This value is not included in settings export. Max 4096 chars.

post-process-prompt.tooltip: Optional custom instruction appended to the selected preset and checkboxes. Max 4096 chars. The transcript, language, context, and vocabulary are added automatically.

artifact-encryption.tooltip: Controls encryption for stored transcript files and retained recording files. Secret Service keyring is the recommended desktop mode. Passphrase mode uses SPEED_OF_CINNAMON_ENCRYPTION_PASSPHRASE_FILE, an existing ~/.config/speed-of-cinnamon/artifact.key, SPEED_OF_CINNAMON_ENCRYPTION_PASSPHRASE, or generates ~/.config/speed-of-cinnamon/artifact.key at runtime when no passphrase source exists. This is also the passphrase fallback for keyring failures. Off stores files as plaintext. Applet transcript export bundles remain encrypted even when stored-artifact encryption is Off.

artifact-encryption-help-keyring.description:
Keyring: Uses the desktop Secret Service and is recommended for normal desktop use.
Fallback and fail closed: If Keyring fails, Speed of Cinnamon falls back to Passphrase and can generate the default key file at runtime. If encryption is selected but no usable key source can be read or generated, stored transcript and recording writes fail closed instead of silently keeping plaintext.
Warning popup: If the backend ever reports that a stored artifact was written without encryption while encryption is expected, the applet shows a critical warning popup.
artifact-encryption-help-keyring.tooltip: Recommended for normal desktop use. Stores the encryption key in the desktop Secret Service and only uses the passphrase fallback when the keyring path fails.

artifact-encryption-help-passphrase.description:
Passphrase: CLI-friendly mode. The key is derived from SPEED_OF_CINNAMON_ENCRYPTION_PASSPHRASE_FILE, an existing ~/.config/speed-of-cinnamon/artifact.key, SPEED_OF_CINNAMON_ENCRYPTION_PASSPHRASE, or a newly generated ~/.config/speed-of-cinnamon/artifact.key when no passphrase source exists.
Weak key handling: A weak default artifact.key is replaced with a newly generated random key at runtime. Weak explicit environment passphrases or explicitly configured passphrase files are rejected instead of being silently overwritten.
Key file requirements: The key file must belong to your user, must not be a symlink, must not be hardlinked, and must use mode 0600 inside a private 0700 directory.
Warning popup: If the backend rejects the passphrase/key file, the applet shows a critical warning popup.
artifact-encryption-help-passphrase.tooltip: Use this for CLI-friendly or portable setups. The default key file is created automatically when no explicit passphrase source is configured.

artifact-encryption-help-off.description:
Off: Stored transcript files and retained recording files are kept as plaintext.
Security impact: Use this only when plaintext transcript and recording files are acceptable. No encryption key, passphrase fallback, or key file is used for stored artifacts. Applet transcript export bundles still use encryption; plaintext export is only available through the CLI with explicit confirmation.
artifact-encryption-help-off.tooltip: Disables encryption for stored transcript and retained recording artifacts.
